- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp spikes; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak if sentiment turns negative.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.00), leading to overshoots in 30d forecast; apply smoothing or lag correction for spikes >10% above mean.
- If sentiment history shows strong negative sentiment followed by a rebound, model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% in early rebound phase.
- For 30d forecasts, if model starts with high values (e.g., >80) and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., -0.5 or lower for 3+ days), model tends to underestimate; add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for pessimism bias.
- When sentiment is mixed or trending toward neutral, model often overcorrects; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
